hotContext.criticalNews: France Transport Minister rejected FSD Supervised as currently configured (speeding + driver monitoring). Consumer FSD Supervised still live only in NL/LT/EE/DK/BE. US NHTSA EA26002 escalated with 'Radar Saves Us' IR (response due Aug 12). No new country approvals this week; total approved consumer markets unchanged at 6 (US + 5 small EU).

recentKeyChanges.title: NHTSA EA26002 escalates: demands Tesla 'Radar Saves Us' internal docs and marketing justification
recentKeyChanges.description: NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation (Director Tanya Topka) sent Tesla a 24-part information request under Engineering Analysis EA26002 (low-visibility FSD crashes), dated July 2 and reported July 21, 2026. Request No. 4 specifically demands all communications, technical docs, test records, and underlying data tied to an internal Tesla document titled 'Radar Saves Us' that Tesla previously submitted during PE24031-01. ODI states the document appears relevant to degradation-detection design and Tesla's understanding of vision-only OEDR limits in the reduced-visibility conditions of nine countable crashes (including one fatality and one injury) across ~3.2 million FSD-capable US vehicles. Other IRs probe 15 marketing statements for overclaiming automation level, the 2024 'FSD Degraded' alert change from red to yellow with chime removed, 'Direct Photon-Count Capability,' Vision Failsafe Ranker, and internal regression metrics. Tesla response deadline: August 12, 2026; civil penalties up to ~$27,874/day for incomplete answers (capped near $139M). Critical framing: EA is the last step before close or recall push. An internal memo named 'Radar Saves Us' implies Tesla analyzed camera-only failure modes that match the crash pattern after removing radar in 2021 — elevating knowledge-of-defect risk. NHTSA EA26002 and Special Crash Investigation remain open; this is escalation of the probe already noted in prior weeks, not a new investigation.

positive_signals: Not a recall order yet — still an information demand within open EA
Tesla has until August 12 to respond and can produce technical rebuttal
NTSB prelim on separate Katy crash previously attributed override to driver (software not primary cause in that case)
negative_signals: Federal IR names internal 'Radar Saves Us' document — implies manufacturer knew vision-only limits relevant to crash conditions
EA26002 covers ~3.2M vehicles, nine reduced-visibility crashes including fatality — last step before possible recall
NHTSA also building marketing overclaim paper trail (15 statements including whiteout/all-conditions claims)
Softened FSD Degraded alert (red→yellow, chime removed) under scrutiny as potential safety-warning defect
Daily civil penalties for incomplete answers; probe not closing
Vision-only stack remains the design under investigation years after radar removal

recentKeyChanges.title: France rejects FSD Supervised: Transport Minister cites speeding and driver-monitoring gaps
recentKeyChanges.description: On or around July 22, 2026, French Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot publicly stated that France will not authorize Tesla Full Self-Driving (Supervised) 'as it currently stands,' saying 'the safety trade-offs are not yet sufficient.' Specific objections: (1) FSD can exceed posted limits to match traffic — Tabarot cited up to ~70 km/h in a 50 km/h zone (~40% over); (2) driver monitoring does not guarantee adequate attention in complex urban maneuvers (lane changes, intersections, roundabouts); (3) French guidelines still expect hands on the wheel. France is refusing to rubber-stamp Dutch RDW national homologation and wants a harmonized EU-wide framework; technical talks with Tesla, the Netherlands, and other member states continue, with a Ministry rep having visited NL data recently and ecosystem meetings planned for autumn. EU-wide mutual-recognition vote still needs 15 member states representing ≥65% of EU population; next potential vote flagged for October. Musk replied on X: 'Delaying the approval of FSD in France will cost lives.' Critical reality: France is a top-tier EU volume market. Consumer FSD Supervised remains live only in five small markets (NL/LT/EE/DK/BE). Germany, France, Italy, Spain, and UK still closed. Tesla's summer-2026 EU-wide mutual-recognition narrative has failed for major markets; France's public rejection plus Sweden's earlier speeding-based opposition raise the bar for October.

positive_signals: France framed this as a delay with fixable conditions, not a permanent ban — technical discussions with Tesla/NL/other states continue
Tabarot said France 'supports these technologies' and is ready to engage if safety bar is met
Specific, addressable issues (speed offset, driver monitoring) rather than blanket opposition to autonomy
Five smaller EU markets (NL/LT/EE/DK/BE) remain live with 50M+ km driven
negative_signals: Official rejection of current FSD Supervised by a major EU auto market's Transport Minister
Concrete safety defects cited: speeding up to ~40% over limit and insufficient urban driver attention
France will not inherit Dutch RDW national approval — undercuts Tesla mutual-recognition shortcut narrative
Germany/France/Italy/Spain/UK still have no consumer FSD Supervised; live footprint remains five small markets
Summer 2026 EU-wide recognition target not delivered; next vote only October and needs 15 states / 65% population
Sweden already urged EU rejection over speeding; France adds a large-population no vote risk for October
Musk 'cost lives' response does not resolve regulatory technical objections

recentKeyChanges.title: FSD v14 Lite goes public for HW3 (2026.20.6.10/.11); HW4 gets point-release v14.3.6 — still Supervised only
recentKeyChanges.description: Tesla restarted and then publicly expanded FSD (Supervised) v14 Lite for HW3/AI3 vehicles with software 2026.20.6.10 (July 20–21), after Ashok Elluswamy said the updated Lite build was 'likely the version that goes to wide release.' NotATeslaApp and TeslaNorth report regular US/Canada HW3 owners beyond early access receiving the OTA; IR shareholder letter confirms v14 Lite delivery began for AI3 customers in the US and South Korea. Official notes: distilled HW4 v14 intelligence into HW3 (RL + offline models), parking/unparking/reversing, Arrival Options, Speed Profiles including SLOTH, optional brake-confirm, Self-Driving app, and streak tracking. Concurrently, 2026.20.6.11 ships FSD Supervised v14.3.6 for HW4 — release notes largely restate the v14.3.5 RL/vision-encoder/MLIR stack with TeslaFi showing ~1.5k cars / ~12% of tracked fleet mid-rollout. Critical reality: this is supervised feature parity and legacy-fleet catch-up, not autonomy progress. Lite is explicitly a distilled student model (slower decision-making than full HW4 v14); HW3 remains permanently capped below unsupervised FSD and is not expected to get v15. Consumer production ceiling is still the v14.3.x branch while robotaxi early-v15 work continues in parallel.

positive_signals: Public HW3 rollout of v14 Lite confirmed by NotATeslaApp, TeslaNorth (US + Canada), and Tesla Q2 IR letter (US + South Korea)
Ashok said updated Lite build is likely the wide-release candidate — rollout advanced beyond early access within ~24 hours
Feature parity gains vs prior HW3: Start from Park, Arrival Options, Speed Profiles, Self-Driving app, streaks, optional brake confirm
HW4 v14.3.6 continuing broader rollout (~11.9% TeslaFi-tracked fleet on 2026.20.6.11)
negative_signals: Still FSD Supervised (SAE L2) only — no unsupervised capability for consumer HW3 or HW4 production software
v14 Lite is a distilled/shrunk model; decision-making slower than full HW4 v14 by design
HW3 permanently excluded from unsupervised FSD and not expected to receive v15 — Lite is effectively the software ceiling until paid hardware upgrades
v14.3.6 is incremental point polish on the same v14.3.x branch covered last week (v14.3.5), not the architectural v15 overhaul
Upcoming Improvements still listed unfixed on v14.3.x notes (expand reasoning beyond destination; pothole avoidance)
